stories.headline: Harry Kane falls short of Cristiano Ronaldo Champions League goal streak record
stories.summary: Harry Kane failed to match Cristiano Ronaldo's record for scoring in the most consecutive Champions League games.
stories.body:
Harry Kane failed to match Cristiano Ronaldo's record for scoring in the most consecutive Champions League games.

Ronaldo's tally of scoring in 11 games in a row still stands after Kane, who had scored in 10 consecutive Champions League appearances, failed to get on the scoresheet on Tuesday against Atlético Madrid.

Bayern Munich beat Atletico 2-0 with goals from Lennart Karl and Konraid Laimer. The second strike came from a Kane assist.

Kane had scored for the 10th Champions League game in succession, and moved one behind the Madrid and Manchester United legend, on matchday three of the campaign with his penalty against Arsenal.

But fresh off claiming the Ballon d'Or, Kane missed out on matching Ronaldo's all-time tally despite helping Bayern win.

Ronaldo's total was set in 2017-18 as Madrid went on to win their third straight Champions League via a memorable victory over Liverpool in the final.

His 11-game run began with a brace against Juventus in the previous year's Champions League final. He then scored in all six group stage matches and in both legs of Madrid's round of 16 and quarterfinal ties.

- Kane says new Bayern deal 'extremely close,' will happen in coming days

Kane's 10-in-a-row run began when he scored twice against Union Saint-Gilloise on matchday seven of Bayern's 2025-26 Champions League campaign. He scored against PSV Eindhoven the following week before watching from the bench as his teammates beat Atalanta 6-1 in Italy in the first leg of their round of 16 meeting.

The former Tottenham Hotspur striker picked up where he left off with two goals in the second leg before finding the back of the net in every game as Bayern's hopes of European glory were ended by Paris Saint-Germain in the semifinals.

Kane has scored against Bodo/Glimt, Viking FK and Arsenal.

Who has scored in the most consecutive Champions League games?

11: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid, 2017-18), Harry Kane (Bayern München, 2026-present)

10: Harry Kane (Bayern München, 2026)

9: Ruud van Nistelrooy (Manchester United, 2002-03)

9: Robert Lewandowski (Bayern München, 2019-20)

9: Robert Lewandowski (Bayern München, 2020-21)

8: Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid, 2013-14)

stories.headline: Gauthier scores 2nd straight hat trick in Ducks’ 5-4 win over Canucks
stories.summary: — Cutter Gauthier scored a hat trick for the second game in a row and the Anaheim Ducks held on for a 5-4 victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday night.
stories.body:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia -- — Cutter Gauthier scored a hat trick for the second game in a row and the Anaheim Ducks held on for a 5-4 victory over the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday night.


Mikael Granlund added a goal and two assists for the Ducks, while Leo Carlsson put away a short-handed tally and Beckett Sennecke had four assists.


Laurent Brossoit stopped 19 shots in the Anaheim net.


The Ducks came into the game with the league’s second-best power play (34%) behind only the Utah Mammoth and went 3 for 3 with the man advantage. Two of Gauthier's goals came on the power play and Anaheim has 10 power-play goals on 12 chances over its last three games.


The Canucks got two goals from Jake DeBrusk, and one each from Liam Ohgren and Linus Karlsson. Elias Pettersson notched a pair of assists. Vancouver goalie Kevin Lankinen made 17 saves.


Granlund opened the scoring with a power-play tally just over four minutes into the first period. Vancouver replied on a man advantage two minutes later. Marco Rossi fed Ohgren just above the crease for the goal.


The Ducks took a 2-1 lead into the intermission when Gauthier fired a shot in on his team’s second power play of the night at the 17:07 mark of the first.


Gauthier also scored three in Anaheim’s 6-3 comeback victory over the Ottawa Senators on Sunday, and is the first player in Ducks history with back-to-back three-goal games.


The 22-year-old American has eight goals in his last three games after going the previous nine without finding the net.


Gauthier was in the penalty box midway through the third when DeBrusk scored his fourth of the season to put the score at 5-3.


DeBrusk breathed new life into Rogers arena with just over 10 minutes left on the game clock, blasting a point shot in to cut Vancouver’s deficit to a single goal.


Up next
Ducks: At the Edmonton Oilers on Thursday.


Canucks: At the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday.

stories.headline: Panthers defenders: We're in 'great hands' after DC switch-up
stories.summary: Promoted from defensive line coach to coordinator, Todd Wash already has the support of the unit's leaders.
stories.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Todd Wash has a second chance at calling plays in the NFL.

The longtime Carolina Panthers defensive line coach was promoted to interim defensive coordinator on Friday following the dismissal of Ejiro Evero, who had been his boss since 2023. Wash -- who served as the Jacksonville Jaguars' defensive coordinator from 2016 to 2020 -- was emotional during his first meeting at the helm, according to several players on Tuesday, as he let the group feel his passion at the front of the room for the first time.

"That first meeting that we had with him, he almost teared up in there," Panthers pass rusher Princely Umanmielen said. "Like you could just really see the passion he has for the game. Just real genuine passion for the game. He got up there and the way he talked to us, the way he presented what the defense is gonna look like, you could just tell how much passion he has and it really makes you want to play hard for him."

Wash, who worked with general manager Dan Morgan and coach Dave Canales in Seattle from 2011 to 2012, was picked to replace Evero because of his experience as a coordinator. He helped lead the Jaguars to the AFC Championship Game following the 2017 season, when Jacksonville had the No. 2 defense in the NFL.

After leaving Jacksonville in 2020, Wash spent the past six seasons working with defensive lines in Detroit and Carolina. He hadn't been on the defensive coordinator search radar over the past few years, and players said they could feel his excitement in regaining the role.

"It really means a lot to him," veteran outside linebacker Patrick Jones II said. "Like you could tell, he was emotional about it. ... And when you see someone go up there and talk like that -- their passion -- it gets you really fired up. ... Like, 'I want to go to war for you. I want to go to war with you.' Cause it really means something when it really means a lot."

Wash oversaw defensive tackle Derrick Brown's lone Pro Bowl season in 2023. The coach and the captain remain tight, and Brown, who had been an outspoken advocate for Evero, said Wash will value the input of his players based on his experience with him.

"He listens to his players, allows you to have a voice and also takes what you have to say into consideration," Brown said. "I think from Day 1 [in 2023] that's the way he's been with me and our room. And you appreciate that as a player."

The bulk of the locker room found out about Evero's dismissal Friday morning away from the facility. Multiple players said they were just waking up after a long, late flight back from Green Bay following the team's 27-19 loss to the Packers.

"Dan Morgan gave me a call -- that was the first person I heard it from, which I really appreciated," longtime Evero pupil and starting safety Nick Scott said. "And the message was -- it was the decision they had to make, I respected it and I know they had a job to do. Wish [passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley] and [Evero] the best of luck, thank them for the role they had in my career to this point, and now we're looking forward to this next game."

"I was genuinely shocked," Umanmielen said. "Like I was genuinely surprised, especially it happening in the middle of the season. Something that I wouldn't have expected at all."

The Panthers enter their Week 9 matchup on Sunday against the Denver Broncos with the league's 23rd-ranked defense, as the unit has given up 349.6 yards per matchup through seven games.

The group also ranks 30th in rushing defense (140.7 yards allowed per game), 29th in sacks percentage (4.56% of dropbacks) and 20th in interception rate (1.66% of pass attempts).

Wash will look to improve those numbers during the final 10 weeks. His background with defensive fronts is likely to lend itself to improving the run defense and pass rush during his interim tenure.

"I guess you could say it's cool because you know he's going to have a little bias there with the D-line," Umanmielen said. "Him being a D-lineman himself, I'm assuming that he would want to see the D-line be successful game in and game out, so it's nice to have a coach with that bias."

The Panthers are on a two-game skid and they're dealing with injuries on defense, including top pass rusher Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and rookie fill-in starting cornerback Will Lee III (hamstring). But their hope is that a new voice at the top of the defense, and perhaps some minor scheme adjustments, can lead to better results.

Wash and the defense will get the opportunity to make a positive reintroduction against Denver's 30th-ranked offense.

"We're in great hands," Scott said. "This is a guy that really cares and loves his job -- is going to pour everything into it, just like we would. So, we have a bunch of guys that are extremely passionate about this game, this sport, this phase of the ball, so we're going to put all of our trust and faith in him, as well as each other, and do whatever we can to continue to build this defense and put this team in positions to win games."

stories.headline: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard completes knee treatment, begins 'return to play process'
stories.summary: Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced.
stories.body:
Kawhi Leonard has completed a treatment to address left knee swelling and is beginning the "return to play process" in Toronto, the Raptors announced Tuesday.

The team said it will provide an update on Leonard's progress in one week, meaning the earliest he could play again would be Nov. 11 against Boston.

Leonard, 35, was sidelined because of left knee swelling after appearing in just two regular-season games for Toronto. An MRI on the knee last month showed no structural damage.

Leonard has previously had issues with his right knee, having multiple surgeries for his meniscus and ACL.

In two games this season, Leonard is averaging 19.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 3.5 steals. He's in his first year back with the Raptors after being traded to Toronto from the LA Clippers this offseason after a scandal-marred conclusion to his six seasons there. He agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors after the trade.

Leonard previously played one season in Toronto, leading the Raptors to their only NBA championship in 2019 before leaving for the Clippers in free agency.

stories.headline: MLB proposes delaying salary cap until 2028 season
stories.summary: Major League Baseball has proposed delaying the implementation of a salary cap until 2028 while it puts into place other elements of its labor offer for 2027.
stories.body:
Major League Baseball on Tuesday proposed postponing the implementation of a salary cap until the 2028 season while still putting into place the other elements of its labor offer for 2027 as the current collective bargaining agreement approaches its Dec. 1 expiration.

With the MLB Players Association consistently voicing its objection to any cap, the league has pressed forward with its pursuit of a cap and floor. But the opening of free agency Monday, and the significant likelihood of MLB locking out the players when the current labor deal expires, complicated the ability of teams to plan amid the uncertain labor landscape and prompted the proposed delay, sources told ESPN.

The $258.2 million cap and $180.2 million floor that the league projected for 2028 in a meeting with the union Tuesday was higher than the $245.3 million and $171.2 million numbers proposed by MLB as its original cap-and-floor offer for 2027. The new numbers reflect a 50-50 split on projected 2028 revenue, with the calculation of player share including hundreds of millions of dollars in amateur signing bonuses as well as deductions by teams that other major men's leagues use in their cap-and-floor systems.

MLB also proposed giving $282 million in competitive balance tax proceeds to players in cash payments, sources said. Players are entitled to 50% of proceeds, according to the current collective bargaining agreement, that are used to fully fund players' 401(k) accounts. IRS limits cap the present-day distribution at around $72 million, according to sources. Because of increased spending beyond the $244 million competitive balance tax threshold, hundreds of millions of dollars in excess owed to players sit in reserve.

Union officials have said players would lose more than $1 billion over the life of the league's proposal if they agreed to a cap, reflecting the chasm between the parties that could lead to a prolonged work stoppage.

MLB locked out players in December 2021, leading to a 99-day stoppage that ended in mid-March 2022. In late May of this year, the league formally proposed a cap-and-floor system for the first time since 1994, when players went on strike for 232 days, the World Series was canceled and baseball returned to the field after players avoided an overhaul to the game's economic system through legal challenges.

Under the league's proposal Tuesday, competitive balance tax thresholds -- a luxury tax mechanism used to penalize teams with higher payrolls -- would remain the same for the 2027 season. While the 2028 cap-and-floor numbers are projections, 12 teams -- including the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers -- would need to increase their payrolls to reach the floor. Eight teams carried payrolls that would have been in excess of the ceiling.

Teams would not be forced to reach the floor in any given year under the league's proposal. They would be permitted to spend as little as 90% of the floor number, as long as over multiple years their spending reflects a minimum agreed-upon number.

The MLBPA has proposed maintaining the current framework of the league's financial system while significantly increasing spending, reflected by a base competitive balance tax threshold of $300 million, a $56 million rise from the current number. Additionally, the union has asked for a surge in the minimum salary from $780,000 to $1.5 million, a $180 million pre-arbitration bonus pool -- it's currently at $50 million -- and free agency for players 30 and older after five years of major league service, not six.

The league, contingent on the acceptance of a cap-and-floor system, has said it would agree to earlier free agency for those 30 and older, while proposing a $900,000 minimum (with some players receiving $1 million) and a $65 million pre-arbitration bonus pool. MLB also has proposed significant changes to amateur entry, implementing an international draft, removing high school players from the domestic draft and slashing domestic draft bonuses, all of which the union opposes.

"Coming off another incredible season of baseball, MLB owners continue to propose blowing up the current system and replacing it with one designed to line their pockets and increase their franchise values," the MLBPA said in a statement. "... Players stand ready to negotiate in good faith toward a new CBA that will capitalize on our sport's unprecedented momentum and benefit players, clubs, and fans alike."

MLB, in a statement explaining its proposal to delay a cap by a year, said it recognized that teams need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap-and-floor system.

"This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system without delaying key player benefits, including earlier free agency, a $1 million minimum salary, a 30% increase to the pre-arbitration bonus pool, and transactional reform that will reduce roster churn," the statement said. "The projected salary cap and floor for 2028 continues to provide more money for major league players while leveling the playing field and giving more teams the ability to participate in the free agent market and retain their homegrown stars so that every fan believes their team has a fair chance to win it all."

stories.headline: Liberty coach Chris DeMarco is out: Next candidates for New York
stories.summary: The Liberty are searching for a coach for a second straight offseason. What went wrong, and what's next?
stories.byline: Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel and Kendra Andrews
stories.body:
Three days after crowning its 2026 champion, the WNBA was back in the news. Chris DeMarco will not be retained as head coach of the New York Liberty, sources told ESPN on Tuesday.

The Liberty will have a third head coach in as many years; the franchise previously moved on from Sandy Brondello in September 2025, one season removed from New York winning its first WNBA title.

"We need to nail this," Liberty general manager Jonathan Kolb said at the time, two months before hiring DeMarco. "If we're going to make a bold decision like this, our players deserve to get the best, and so we'll take the time necessary."

DeMarco came to Brooklyn after spending over a decade on staff with the Golden State Warriors and serving as head coach of the Bahamas men's basketball team since 2019.

His one season in New York was rather rocky. The Liberty won the Commissioner's Cup in late June but were 13-12 just before the All-Star break. They finished the season 26-18 -- their worst win percentage in a season since signing Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones in 2023 -- and earned the eighth and final seed in the playoffs, where they swept the No. 1 Minnesota Lynx but then were swept in turn by the No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream in the semifinals.

This is the third consecutive offseason that a WNBA coach has been let go after one year; it happened with Teresa Weatherspoon in Chicago (2024) and Chris Koclanes in Dallas (2025). But DeMarco is the first noninterim coach to win a playoff series in his first season and not return to coach the same team.

But New York has sky-high internal and external expectations. After the Liberty were eliminated in the semis -- a second straight year without a Finals appearance -- the Liberty's stars reiterated their desire to not just compete for championships but win them. So what's next for New York as the franchise looks for a new coach for the second offseason in a row? ESPN analyzes how the Liberty got here and how they move forward.

What went wrong for DeMarco in his first season?
Philippou: On paper, firing a coach who went 26-18 and swept the No. 1 seed in the first round of the playoffs might seem surprising, but it felt like this was the outcome New York was headed toward especially given how its season ended -- and with none of the Liberty's stars going to bat for their coach.

It seemed like there was a legitimate learning curve with DeMarco and his staff's first season in the WNBA. He spoke in his introductory news conference about ordering every book on the Liberty and having to learn about the history of the WNBA. And while he had experience as head coach of the Bahamas national team, coaching in sporadic FIBA windows is not the same as the grind of a 44-game regular season.

It was notable that Stewart critiqued the team for being too inconsistent this year. "This is not like cramming for a test. You got to be ready and ready to go since the jump," she said in response to a question about DeMarco's future.

There were some positives, like how DeMarco reset the Liberty's offense -- they were one of the better offensive teams in the league in the second half of the season. But even once Leonie Fiebich returned from injury, they were far from an elite defensive team, needed to be a true contender.

It often felt like Stewart took on more of a burden in leading the team than DeMarco. That was especially evident in how she was the one who spoke out the most after Game 2 of the semifinals, when the Liberty thought officials said they did not have a reset timeout to use at the end of overtime when they actually had one. Even in the aftermath, Sabrina Ionescu took more public accountability than DeMarco for not stopping the game to get clarity on whether New York had the timeout.

New York would not make the decision to part ways with DeMarco if it had felt Year 2 would be better than Year 1 under a new head coach. We'll see what the organization has in mind for its next hire, but it seems it did not have enough faith he could grow into the leader it needed by next season.

Andrews: There were a lot of moments leading up to Tuesday's move, but the lasting image of DeMarco's stint in New York is the blundered reset timeout Alexa mentions above. That mishandling of the closing seconds led to a crucial loss, but perhaps even more striking was the response afterwards. Instead of DeMarco taking ownership of his mistake, the players spoke up. It was a strange peek inside the leadership of the Liberty, and it felt like a nail in the coffin.

There were questions about how much knowledge DeMarco had about the WNBA since he was introduced as the head coach last winter. And that moment in the playoffs felt like a prime example of his lack of experience in the WNBA.

Voepel: Maybe DeMarco didn't realize how fast Kolb would pull the plug on him, so he thought he would have more time to adjust to the WNBA. But we can look at something Kolb said last year when the Liberty parted with Brondello.

"This is not a results-based organization," Kolb said in late September 2025 in explaining the decision. "This is not about not winning or winning. It's about how do we position ourselves to be at the top of the league in a real sustainable way as the league evolves."

In short, it seemed like Kolb didn't believe Brondello was innovative enough for a changing league. He apparently believed DeMarco was, but that didn't turn out to Kolb's and the Liberty's satisfaction, either.

So, whoever takes this job next has to understand what Kolb wants in terms of everyday results (which do matter) and also what meets the GM's definition of "sustainable" innovation. DeMarco probably thought he would get more of a chance to prove himself in both respects.

Who are the early candidates to be New York's next coach?

Voepel: In 2024, Brondello led the Liberty to the first WNBA championship in the organization's then 28-year history. After a first-round playoff exit in 2025, she was let go, despite seeming to have the support of Stewart. Now DeMarco is out. How does all that impact how appealing this job is?

One avenue for New York is a former NBA assistant. Becky Hammon (Las Vegas) and Natalie Nakase (Golden State) both came from those ranks, and both have won championships as WNBA head coaches. Hammon even played 16 seasons in the WNBA.

Accordingly, one name could be Los Angeles Lakers assistant coach Lindsey Harding, the former Duke star who was the WNBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2007. She played nine seasons in the WNBA, then began her coaching career as a scout and development coach with the Philadelphia 76ers. She also had a stint with the Sacramento Kings before joining the Lakers. It would seem likely that the Liberty will at least gauge her interest.

Another path could be what the Atlanta Dream did with Karl Smesko: Going to the college ranks to find a coach who knows the women's game well and is ready to move to the pro ranks. But, again, job security (or lack thereof) could be an obstacle.

Philippou: To Voepel's point, hiring someone who lacked familiarity with the WNBA and women's basketball came back to bite New York, so Kolb could target someone who checks those boxes. He could look at a NBA or WNBA assistant ready for a head coach role, but that begs the question of whether an inexperienced head coach is the right fit for this title-minded group and a limited championship window.

New York likes to go big, so it wouldn't be shocking for them to check in with the likes of Hammon and Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White. (Nakase would have been on that list too had the Valkyries not literally just won a championship.)

In addition to finding a new coach, what are the other offseason priorities for the franchise?

Philippou: It is quite possible the Liberty's roster will look fairly different in 2027. Stewart, Jones, Ionescu, Fiebich and Satou Sabally all remain under contract, as does French rookie Marine Fauthoux, who had a breakout semifinal series against the Dream.

New York will want an update on the status of Sabally, who had to step away from the court this summer to deal with the effects of her second concussion in a year. There has been no word publicly on when she might return to the court.

Ionescu also had a tough year health-wise, so this season will be all about her getting healthy. Her struggles in 2026 put much more of a burden on Stewart, especially, to be great every single night; but, longer term, Stewart will need more help if this team wants to win another championship.

That said, most of the Liberty's supporting cast will be free agents this offseason, including Pauline Astier, Marine Johannes and Han Xu. It wouldn't be shocking to see Kolb overhaul the bench and look to bolster the team's wing depth.

In the wake of the Liberty's semifinal elimination, New York players spoke more generally about what they want to see in future roster construction.

"It just took a while to find our identity, what we were going to do defensively and how we were going to play with teams," Stewart said. "When people say defense wins championships, it's f---ing true."

Added Fiebich, who lamented the loss of Nyara Sabally and Kayla Thornton in the last two expansion drafts: "We won in 2024 because we brought the toughness and we had the talent and we had the team chemistry. I think we've got to continue to find ways to get that back."

stories.headline: Robert Lewandowski's jersey outselling Lionel Messi's since Chicago arrival
stories.summary: Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in MLS since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Miami kit.
stories.body:
Robert Lewandowski's Chicago Fire jersey has been the most popular in Major League Soccer since his arrival to the league in June, outselling even Lionel Messi's Inter Miami kit.

MLS' 10 best-selling jerseys of 2026 was revealed by the league on Tuesday, with Messi still No. 1 overall but with former Barcelona and Bayern Munich star Lewandowski making a big impact.

- MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up

- Messi brings Miami back to stun Revs, clinch Champions Cup spot

- Nashville ties Miami's single-season points record with 1 game to go

Lewandowski officially signed with Chicago on June 29, and made his MLS debut on July 22 against Inter Miami.

The Poland international has recorded seven goals and added five assists in 18 games, propelling the Fire to fourth place on the Eastern Conference table and a place in the playoffs.

Miami captain Messi, however, leads sales through all of 2026, earning first place for the fourth consecutive season. Messi first topped the list in 2023, just months after signing with Inter Miami in July of that year.

This year, just behind Messi, LAFC's Son Heung-Min stands in second place and Vancouver Whitecaps forward Thomas Müller in third.

The list was based on sales made on MLS' online store from Jan. 1 through Oct. 30.

New Orlando City player Antoine Griezmann made the list in fifth place after being announced as a new signing in March but officially joining MLS in July upon completing the 2025-26 season with Atlético Madrid.

In sixth place was rising United States star Cavan Sullivan's Philadelphia Union jersey. Sullivan, 17, became the youngest scorer for the U.S. men's national team last month when he found the net against Mexico.

stories.headline: Luana Santos comes to grips with rise in women's bantamweight rankings
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Luana Santos stuck with her strongest fighting skill -- grappling -- in Saturday's UFC fight with fellow top-10 women's bantamweight Yana Santos. Her perseverance paid off. After all nine of her takedown attempts were fended off in the first round, Santos went right back to leaning on her judo background in the two rounds that followed, landing five takedowns and amassing 7½ minutes of control time and winning her fourth fight in a row.

As a result, Luana Santos climbs two spots to No. 5 in the ESPN women's bantamweight rankings, while previously fifth-ranked Yana Santos drops one position to No. 6.

That is the only change in the latest divisional rankings. Women's bantamweight does have change on the horizon, though, as UFC champion Kayla Harrison, unranked because she has not fought in over a year and is ineligible, takes on former two-division champion Amanda Nunes on Nov. 14 at UFC 334. Nunes is coming off a retirement of nearly 3½ years.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton: Watching successor Kimi Antonelli win title 'highlight of my year'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton has said watching his Mercedes successor Kimi Antonelli win his first world championship was the "highlight" of his Formula 1 season.

Antonelli, who replaced the seven-time world champion at Mercedes at the start of 2025 following his move to Ferrari, clinched the title at Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, becoming the youngest champion in F1 history at just 20 years old.

Hamilton, along with fellow multiple title-winner Max Verstappen, celebrated Antonelli's achievement on the podium and praised the Italian in a post on social media on Monday.

"Let me start with a huge congratulations to the new champion, Kimi Antonelli," Hamilton, 41, wrote on Instagram. "To have seen your journey so closely and to be there celebrating with you, was a highlight of my year. So well deserved and a record that will stand for a long time.

"It was great to see your team at Mercedes celebrating with you. Enjoy this moment, keep your family close, keep your passion and your energy."

Antonelli was just 18 when he stepped into Hamilton's seat at Mercedes, facing the daunting task of replacing the most successful driver in F1 history, who won six of his seven world titles with the Silver Arrows.

But the Italian has enjoyed a remarkable second season, beating teammate George Russell and Ferrari's Hamilton -- among others -- to the championship with four rounds still scheduled to take place.

Hamilton's congratulations came alongside an admission of frustration over Ferrari's weekend in Mexico, where he felt the team had missed an opportunity to win and also appeared to acknowledge tensions following Charles Leclerc's actions on the opening laps.

"Our own weekend was one full of challenges," Hamilton said. "We had a lot thrown at us but our mechanics and engineers did an incredible job.

"We've grown so much together this year, and that progress has taken a huge effort from everyone on the track and back at the factory. That's why losing what could've been a win hurts so much.

"We need to grasp every opportunity we have, so it's incredibly frustrating, and I can't pretend otherwise."

- Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari have 'big problems' after Charles Leclerc incident

- Hamilton demands 'serious talks' at Ferrari, questions Leclerc's 'mentality'

He added: "Battling is necessary, but when that battle costs the team, we have to be honest about it and learn from it.

"We can push each other to the limit and still honour the responsibility to everyone who put us on that track."

Despite his frustrations, Hamilton insisted his commitment to Ferrari remained unchanged.

"I'll keep giving everything I have. My belief in this team hasn't changed and neither has my responsibility to help us get this right," he said.

"Stick with us. I'm only just getting started with this team, and we have so much more to come."

stories.headline: Chris Fagan to join the Blues as director of coaching in 2027
stories.summary: Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.
stories.body:
Triple premeirship coach Chris Fagan has made the call on his AFL future, joining Carlton as their director of coaching for 2027.

The 65-year-old stepped down as Brisbane's senior coach after the club's 2026 premiership win -- it's third in a row -- with an aim to return closer to family.

Announced by the Blues on Saturday morning, Fagan will oversee a matchday role and begin mentoring the coaching panel to "establish development pathways for the coaches and help drive an elite, sustainable football program".

Fagan said he was looking forward to making a "real impact" at the Blues.

"While I loved my 10 years as a Senior Coach, this is a role I am passionate about and where I know I can have a real impact in this next phase of my football career," Fagan said in a statement.

"Supporting people to get the absolute best out of themselves is what I love most about football, so the chance to now be able to do that on a full-time basis is incredibly exciting. I can't wait to connect with each person in the football department, and in particular work closely with Josh to help every coach and player be the best Carlton person they can possibly be.

"In all my conversations with [the club] before accepting the role, what resonated strongly was how aligned they were on how to make Carlton a great football club. They shared a clear vision of evolving Carlton into a club that can contend but most importantly, they understand there is still significant work to do to get there.

"To have the senior leadership of a football club share such clarity in their direction, combined with a role that gives me genuine purpose, makes joining Carlton an opportunity too good to pass up."

Meanwhile Carlton's GM of Football Chris Davies said the appointment was an important one to support first-time senior coach Josh Fraser.

"We want to build our football club around good people and they do not come any better than Chris Fagan," Davies said.

"Few in the game have his wealth of experience and ability to connect with and get the best out of those around him. Most importantly, he is a proven winner who knows what it takes to build a consistently high-performing environment.

"Chris and Josh have built a connection in recent weeks over a shared philosophy of putting people first and building a program the right way. With Chris on board, Josh will be well supported, our coaches will be well developed and our program will continue to build the clarity and discipline required to be truly elite.

"We can't wait to welcome Chris and his wife Ursula, their daughters Jessica and Ellen and the entire Fagan family to Carlton."

...more to come.

stories.headline: NRL transfer whispers: Cowboys keen on Raiders' Savage
stories.summary: The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1. Isaac Issa has news on Bradman Best's future and which clubs might be lining up a play for Sam Walker.
stories.body:
The NRL season may be over, but the player market is already heating up ahead of November 1, with clubs beginning to shape their rosters for 2027 and beyond.

From player movement to changes behind the scenes, ESPN NRL Insider Isaac Issa has the latest whispers from around the competition.

Cowboys among clubs eyeing Savage

North Queensland are among the clubs showing interest in Canberra winger Xavier Savage, as rivals assess their recruitment options for 2028.

ESPN understands the Cowboys and a Sydney-based club are keeping tabs on the speedster, who is contracted to the Raiders until the end of 2027 and became eligible to negotiate with rivals on November 1.

Savage scored 13 tries in 19 NRL appearances for Canberra this season.

Bryenton begins Tigers chapter

David Bryenton will begin full-time training with the Wests Tigers on Wednesday, with ESPN understanding the recruit features in Benji Marshall's long-term plans.

Having first reported his signing last month, ESPN can reveal Bryenton's mutually agreed release from the Bulldogs has now been finalised, clearing the way for him to join Marshall's squad for pre-season.

Dolphins win race for Su'a

The Dolphins have won the race to retain Sebastian Su'a, with ESPN understanding the young forward has agreed to terms on a two-year extension that will keep him in Redcliffe until the end of 2029.

Several NRL clubs had identified Su'a as a potential recruitment target, but the Dolphins have moved to secure his future with the club.

Fa'alogo agrees to long-term Storm extension

Sua Fa'alogo has agreed to extend his stay at the Melbourne Storm through to the end of 2032, ESPN understands.

The agreement will keep the fullback in Melbourne for the next six seasons, securing a key figure in the Storm's long-term plans.

Fa'alogo's retention delivers a major boost for Melbourne ahead of the November 1 contracting window, with the club moving to lock down one of its most exciting talents.

Dolphins close in on Lemuelu extension, confident of keeping Farnworth

The Dolphins are closing in on a multi-year extension for Connelly Lemuelu as they also express confidence in retaining Herbie Farnworth.

ESPN understands Lemuelu is nearing an agreement to extend his stay despite interest from Canberra, Parramatta and Cronulla.

Securing the back-rower would deliver a retention boost for the Dolphins, with the length of the proposed deal yet to be confirmed.

The club is also understood to be confident it can retain Farnworth despite links to the Sydney Roosters.

While that confidence is yet to translate into a confirmed extension, keeping the English international alongside Lemuelu would help preserve key combinations on the Dolphins' left edge.

Eels edge ahead in Best race
Parramatta have emerged as the frontrunners to land Bradman Best, with multiple sources indicating the Newcastle centre is increasingly likely to join the Eels beyond 2027.

Best has been identified as a priority target for Parramatta, who are looking to bolster Jason Ryles' backline with an established representative star.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the Eels are understood to be in the box seat despite Newcastle's efforts to retain him with a lucrative extension.

Bulldogs unlikely to enter Walker race
Canterbury are unlikely to enter the race for Sam Walker, with the Bulldogs backing their existing halfback options ahead of the upcoming season.

Despite suggestions the club could emerge as a potential destination for Walker, it is understood Canterbury are taking a wait-and-see approach rather than preparing to launch a pursuit.

The Bulldogs' immediate focus remains on the internal battle for the No.7 jersey, with Mitch and Alex Conti set to compete for the role over the offseason.

Canterbury have not completely shut the door on a move should circumstances change, but their current position suggests they are unlikely to become an active contender for Walker's signature.

For now, the Bulldogs are content to watch how the situation unfolds.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal want Atlético Madrid winger
stories.summary: Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena has caught the eye of Arsenal, while Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Arsenal are keeping tabs on Atlético Madrid winger Álex Baena, TEAMtalk reports. An offer worth €80 million is expected to be required to secure the 25-year-old's transfer, as the Gunners explore the market for a top option to play on the left flank. The Premier League side could face competition from Bayern Munich for Baena, who has scored five goals and provided three assists in 11 LaLiga matches this season. Arsenal could raise funds for this with the exit of midfielder Martín Zubimendi, amid interest from Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old has struggled to start regularly since the arrival of Bruno Guimarães and the Gunners would want a fee around the €60 million that they parted with to land him from Real Sociedad in July 2025.

- Juventus are weighing up approaches for Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko and AS Monaco forward Folarin Balogun, with plans to land a striker in January, Calciomercato reports. The Serie A club are keen to acquire a physical front man in the next transfer window, when they are expected to have around €100 million available to reinforce their squad. Šeško, 23, hasn't featured for United since Sept. 16 in the EFL Cup against Brighton due to injury, while a move for 25-year-old Balogun could be possible after Monaco accepted an initial €40 million offer from Everton in the summer before the deal fell through.

- Manchester United are considering a move for Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney as they prioritize adding depth at the No. 9 position, according to Football Insider. The Red Devils are monitoring the 30-year-old, who has scored 12 goals in nine Saudi Pro League matches this season, with several other options also on their shortlist. Toney has been in Saudi Arabia since joining Al Ahli from Brentford in the summer of 2024.

- Barcelona are interested in Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall, according to Football Insider. Bergvall, 20, chose Spurs over Barcelona in 2024, but the Blaugrana are still monitoring him, though Spurs are in control of his future as his contract is not set to expire until the summer of 2031. The Sweden international has made four Premier League appearances this season and has also emerged on the radar of Napoli.

- Al-Hilal have ended their pursuit of Manchester United midfielder Bruno Fernandes, TalkSPORT reports. The Saudi Pro League club were strongly linked with a move for the 32-year-old over the summer, but they aren't expected to make a new approach for him in January, with no plans to free up any of their overseas player slots. Fernandes, yet to reach an agreement over a new contract at Old Trafford, has eight months remaining on his deal.

Other rumors
- Manchester United are interested in Manchester City left back Rayan Aït-Nouri. (Florian Plettenberg)

- Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain have made recent inquiries for Chelsea winger Estêvão. (TEAMtalk)

- Benfica are interested in Monza striker Gustavo Varela, 21, but there is strong competition emerging from Arsenal, Napoli and Barcelona. (A Bola)

- AC Milan have joined the race for Club Brugge striker Nicolò Tresoldi. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Minnesota United forward Kelvin Yeboah is on the radar of Everton. (Football Insider)

- USMNT defender George Campbell is in talks with West Brom regarding a contract extension. (Mike McGrath)

- Sunderland midfielder Noah Sadiki is attracting interest from Liverpool, Newcastle, Napoli, and Juventus. (Ekrem Konur)

- Brighton remain keen on FC Köln winger Said El Mala. (Florian Plettenberg)

- Liverpool will look to offload attacking midfielder Harvey Elliott if Valencia terminate his current loan in January. (Football Insider)

- Monza and Pisa are exploring loan moves for AC Milan forward Francesco Camarda. (Nicolò Schira)

stories.headline: Ex-NFL QB Russell Wilson interviews with NC State for head coaching job
stories.summary: Russell Wilson interviewed for the head coaching job at NC State on Tuesday, joining Philip Rivers as prominent candidates, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
Former Super Bowl champion quarterback Russell Wilson interviewed Tuesday for the head coaching job at NC State, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Wilson, 38, joins Philip Rivers as former NC State and NFL quarterbacks who are now prominent candidates for the Wolfpack job. NC State fired Dave Doeren as head coach on Oct. 24.

Wilson played at NC State from 2008 to 2010 before transferring to Wisconsin in 2011. After being taken by Seattle in the third round of the 2012 NFL draft, he went on to play 14 seasons in the NFL, leading the Seahawks to their first Super Bowl championship in the 2013 season.

A 10-time Pro Bowl selection, Wilson announced in June that he was retiring from the NFL to become an analyst with CBS Sports.

Rivers, who played at NC State from 2000 to 2003, is in his sixth season as coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Fairhope, Alabama. River led the Cardinals to the state playoff semifinals in the previous two seasons.

The 44-year-old Rivers, who has never coached in college, has told NC State that he wants to finish the current high school season, sources told ESPN.

stories.headline: Dumonts take over as controlling owners of Mavericks
stories.summary: Sivan and Patrick Dumont purchased Miriam Adelson's shares of the Mavericks last month, making the Dumont family the controlling owners of the franchise.
stories.body:
Sivan and Patrick Dumont purchased Miriam Adelson's shares of the Dallas Mavericks last month, making the Dumont family the controlling owners of the franchise with a 69% share.
Adelson has had minimal involvement with the Mavericks since she bought the majority share of the franchise from Mark Cuban in December 2023 along with her daughter and son-in-law. Patrick Dumont has served as the Mavericks' governor since the families took control of the franchise.

"It's really about long-term investment in the city of Dallas," Dumont told ESPN on Tuesday. "The Dumont family is really committed to building what we hope is the best arena in the NBA, a really significant investment in the city that will help create the new 40-year home for the Dallas Mavericks, a great experience for our fans and inspire our team to win championships. That's really what we're focused on. We had the opportunity, and we're really excited about it."

Cuban, who has expressed regret about selling the Mavericks to Adelson and the Dumonts due to being frozen out of the franchise's basketball and business operations, maintains a 27% share of the franchise. According to the terms of the 2023 sale, Dumont can purchase another 20% share from Cuban at the original $3.5 billion valuation.

"Our plan is to look at that and to do that over time," Dumont said. "I just have to tell you: I love Mark. He's been a great family friend for a really long time. He's just a super passionate Mavs fan and he's frustrated. I respect it. We're going to hopefully do him proud. That's my goal -- to make all of our Mavs fans super proud about the success of the team and win a championship."

Dumont, the Las Vegas Sands Co. CEO, has overseen a major overhaul of the franchise during his turbulent tenure as the Mavericks governor.

Dumont drew intense wrath from the fanbase for approving former general manager Nico Harrison's decision to trade perennial MVP candidate Luka Doncic to the Los Angeles Lakers months after the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals. Dumont has since taken drastic measures to attempt to position the franchise for success as it pivots to build around Cooper Flagg, the reigning Rookie of the Year who Dallas drafted with the No. 1 overall pick after a historic stroke of lottery luck.

"The most important thing every day is just trying to work harder to get better," Dumont said. "It's something that really applies in life, but it's something that really applies to here. It's been an experience as a new owner in the league. Dallas is a great sports city. I think we have the best fans in the NBA, very passionate, and it's my job to make sure that we win and that we support our fans. I'm really focused on that. I've learned that there are a lot of things you can do -- sometimes they work, sometimes they don't -- but you've got to keep pushing, got to keep going."

Dumont, who fired Harrison last November, hired championship-proven former Toronto Raptors executive Masai Ujiri as president in May and authorized Ujiri to make sweeping changes throughout the front office and coaching staff.

"This is Masai Ujiri's team," Dumont said. "He's got a ring. He knows what he's doing."

Ujiri parted ways with former coach Jason Kidd and replaced him with Dusty May, who had just led Michigan to a national championship. Ujiri also hired general manager Mike Schmitz, who had been the assistant general manager for the Portland Trail Blazers.

"I'm really proud of our team," Dumont said. "I think it starts on the basketball side with Masai Ujiri. He's a supreme talent. He's a great person with very high character. He works very hard. He's very focused on accountability and creating a winning team and creating a culture of success. It started with him."

Dumont has also made hires in eight of the 11 senior leadership positions in the franchise's business operations over the last two years.

Dumont recruited Naismith Hall of Fame executive Rick Welts out of retirement, hiring Welts in 2025 as CEO to help guide the franchise through a significant transformation, including planning for a new arena to open in 2031. Welts plans to retire again at the end of the calendar year and will be succeed by team president Ethan Casson, who joined the Mavericks in August 2025 after a nine-year tenure as the CEO of the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx.

"I've seen this movie before," said Welts, who led the Chase Center project during his decade-long tenure with the Golden State Warriors during that franchise's dynasty era. "I can't guarantee championships, but this [franchise] is destined for great success because of the leadership that Patrick has put in place on the business and basketball sides."

The Mavericks' practice facility underwent an offseason renovation with at an eight-figure cost. A highlight of the renovation was the re-design and expansion of the dining area, creating the Champions Performance Kitchen in collaboration with the 50 Eggs Hospitality Group, providing players, coaches and staff an elite restaurant-caliber culinary experience and personalized performance nutrition.

The team's business offices are currently undergoing an eight-figure renovation.

The anticipation is that the franchise will have a new business office and practice facility when the Mavericks' new arena is scheduled to open in five years. The franchise entered into an option agreement this summer to purchase a 104-acre tract at the former Valley View Mall site in north Dallas, and the process of re-zoning to allow for the construction of an arena at that site is underway.

"I'm feeling great about where we are in terms of creating the best building ever created for basketball," Welts said. "From a design perspective, we're way ahead of schedule. Patrick is very involved in that. Patrick has taken it to a different level. Patrick's interest in all things related to hospitality is unlike anything I've ever seen before. He builds the best hotels and resorts in the world. That's his day job, understanding how to build a premium hospitality experience. He's more involved in the building of this arena than any owner I can imagine."

Dumont oversaw the construction of the Venetian Arena in Macao, China, which is two years into a five-year deal to host the NBA's preseason China Games. That building is a 12,000-seat arena with elements of a luxury resort. Dumont's plan is incorporate similar luxury touches into a larger arena with Texas style elements in Dallas.

"That was something we couldn't do to the scale that we can do in Dallas," Dumont said. "I think what we bring to Dallas is going to be world class. My goal is to make the best arena in the NBA. It starts with the court and expands outwards, and I want to make sure the fans have the best experience possible, because we owe it to them."

stories.headline: Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he regrets anti-Yankees comments to Jake Bauers
stories.summary: Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he regrets his recent comments to Jake Bauers about the Yankees, adding that he didn't intend to "slander" the Bronx Bombers.
stories.body:
Milwaukee Brewers manager Pat Murphy says he regrets his recent comments to Jake Bauers about the New York Yankees, adding that he didn't intend to "slander" the Bronx Bombers.

Murphy addressed his anti-Yankees barb with the New York Post's "The Show" podcast, which posted its interview with the Milwaukee manager Tuesday, six days after the Brewers won the first World Series title in franchise history.

As he celebrated with Bauers on the field after the Brewers' series-clinching Game 5 victory, Murphy mentioned "that horses--- Yankees team" where "you guys were all playing for yourself." The moment was captured on video and went viral last week.

Murphy told "The Show" that he contacted Brian Cashman and had a "good conversation" with the longtime Yankees general manager.

"I called Brian Cashman right away when I heard [my comments] got out," said Murphy, who added that he didn't realize he was "on a hot mic" during his exchange with Bauers.

"I tried to explain that I wasn't talking about the 2026 Yankees. I was just referring to the teams with a lot of money that sign a lot of players that sometimes end up not being that 'Little Engine that Could,' so to speak -- more of a high expectation, 'I gotta get mine.' I regret saying it."

Bauers, who played for the Yankees in 2023, caught the final out in Milwaukee's 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays. The brief conversation with Murphy started as the Brewers were celebrating on the field at Tropicana Field and Bauers presented Murphy with the ball from the series-clinching play.

"You're going to be a rich f---er," Murphy told Bauers, who is scheduled to become a free agent this offseason. "Just remember when you were on that horses--- Yankees team and you guys were all playing for yourself? Just remember, say, 'This is the way we used to do it.'"

Murphy told "The Show" that those remarks were consistent with the "rhetoric" he used with Bauers throughout Milwaukee's championship run.

"After every celebration, I'd shake his hand and I'd say, 'You rich so-and-so, you're going to leave us,'" Murphy said. "We're not going to be able to pay you. You're going to leave us, and you're going to forget all about how we did things. ... I would just give him this rhetoric every time."

Bauers enjoyed a breakout 2026 season, his third in Milwaukee since being traded to the Brewers by the Yankees in November 2023. He appeared in 84 games with New York that year, batting .202 with 12 home runs and 95 strikeouts in 272 plate appearances.

But Bauers has rejuvenated his career with the Brewers and posted career bests in virtually every offensive category in 2026, including batting average (.266), homers (26), RBIs (86) and OPS (.874). He was named MVP of Milwaukee's National League Championship Series victory over the Dodgers after batting .286 with six RBIs in the Brewers' four-game series sweep.

As for the Yankees, Murphy reiterated that he merely meant to reference a high-payroll team and that he was not singling them out.

"I felt horribly if I slandered the Yankees, because I was just kind of referring to them as this iconic machine. ... It wasn't smart on my part, and I'm sorry about it," he said.

stories.headline: 2027 WNBA championship odds: Lynx, Aces ahead of Dream, Valkyries
stories.summary: An early look at the odds to win the 2027 WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
After coming into the 2026 season as 45-1 underdogs to win the WNBA Finals, the Golden State Valkyries will be among the favorites to win the title in 2027, though there is little consensus across the sportsbook marketplace.

The Valkyries are the favorites to win the 2027 WNBA Finals at BetMGM, showing +300 odds ... but at DraftKings, the Minnesota Lynx -- who notched the 2026 regular season's best record -- are the favorites at +310, while Caesars Sportsbook and FanDuel have the Las Vegas Aces favored at +340 and +360, respectively. The 2026 runner-up Atlanta Dream are within the top four at all the sportsbooks, showing a short of +400 at DraftKings.

Just outside the top tier are Caitlin Clark's Indiana Fever (+900 at DraftKings) and Paige Bueckers' Dallas Wings, who are a relatively long 14-1 at DraftKings, but are as short as +750 at BetMGM. There's also a wide range of odds on the New York Liberty, who are anywhere between +900 and 17-1 for the 2027 title after a relatively disappointing 2026 campaign that saw them come in as title favorites.

For all of the potential contenders at the top of the board, there is also a cadre of long shots at the bottom, with the Chicago Sky, Seattle Storm, Toronto Tempo and relocating Houston Comets all coming in at 120-1, per DraftKings lines.

Odds by DraftKings and subject to change.

stories.headline: MLS Power Rankings: Miami finds its feet with Decision Day coming up
stories.summary: Which teams are in the best position heading into Decision Day? All this and more in the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings.
stories.body:
It's Monday and another weekend of action is in the books. With Decision Day coming up next week, it's time for the latest edition of ESPN's MLS Power Rankings to see which teams are in a good or bad spot to qualify for the MLS Cup playoffs.

1. Nashville SC
Previous ranking: 1

While seeking history on a rainy night in Tennessee, Nashville fell behind by two goals, had multiple goals called off, but battled back to force two own goals and clinch a 3-2 win against Red Bull New York with stoppage-time headed goal from Sam Surridge. The Supporters' Shield winners are level with Miami's points record, but could break it with just a point from their final game.

2. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 2

Miami reclaimed second place in the Eastern Conference with a second-half rally against the Revs to win 2-1, ignited by the guy still leading the Golden Boot race: Lionel Messi. After a headed assist to Germán Berterame to level the score, Messi scored his 26th goal of the year after finagling past multiple defenders then sending a low left-footed strike past Matt Turner.

3. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 4

The Revs' four-game win streak came to a halt against the Herons, as Messi proved the difference maker once more assisting and scoring in a come-from-behind win for Miami. With that, New England drops to third place in the Eastern Conference. Silver lining? Dániel Gazdag is now on a two-game scoring streak.

4. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 3

STL had the firepower in the attacking third to come away with all three points against San Diego. But thanks in part to Pablo Sisniega's six saves and Anders Dreyer's moment of quality, they went home with a 1-0 defeat instead. The playoffs were already locked up but home-field advantage isn't as they head into the final weekend.

5. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 5

After going scoreless in six games, Robert Lewandowski came off the bench to make the difference in Colorado, providing the go-ahead goal 10 minutes after subbing on, then setting up Puso Dithejane for the 4-2 win.

6. Vancouver Whitecaps
Previous ranking: 7

The Whitecaps showed their quality in a comprehensive 5-1 dismantling of Seattle, highlighted by a Brian White brace that started in the 56th minute. After a 4-1 win over San Diego in midweek and 29th-place Montréal up next, the Western Conference's first-place side have got some momentum ahead of the postseason.

7. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 6

After drawing Nashville 0-0 in the midweek, Philly's 1-0 loss to Cincinnati is their second in three games. They'll be in the postseason, but they may have a tough matchup when it comes.

8. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 9

With the Golden Boot technically still in reach, Petar Musa (who scored 22 goals this season) missed his first penalty in six this season in the 97th minute. Stefan Cleveland's late-game save kept the Toros from three points in a 1-1 draw as they head into the final weekend looking to secure second place in the Western Conference.

9. LAFC
Previous ranking: 8

After losing 3-1 to Minnesota, LAFC are winless in three (two draws) ahead of a Decision Day battle with the Sounders. With their playoff place secure, they're competing for a better finish in the standings, but will fall short of their top-three finish in the Western Conference in the last four seasons.

10. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

Kristijan Kahlina, whose save percentage (75.9%) is second only to first-place Nashville's Brian Schwake (77.7%), stopped eight against Orlando in a match that ended 4-0 in Charlotte's favor, despite both teams firing off the same number of shots (and nearly the same on target, though Charlotte had higher quality opportunities).

11. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 11

After losing 4-0 to mid-table side Charlotte, Orlando picked up their first defeat in six games but still clinched their playoff spot based on other results. They're in the final wild card spot ahead of a final test against the Revs.

12. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 15

The Quakes took 17 minutes to score twice against RSL, and that was enough to secure three points in a 2-1 win. That's their first win in six (four draws, one loss) as they look to secure their third-place spot in the Western Conference.

13. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 10

In a 5-1 loss to Vancouver, Jordan Morris' brief light of life in the second half was overshadowed by the Whitecaps' rapid response in a match characterized by goalkeeper Andy Thomas looking painfully skyward for help from the scoreline. After losing to Houston in midweek, the Sounders have three defeats and no wins from their last five games. They play LAFC on the final day while sitting one place short of the wild card spots.

14. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 14

Morgan Whittaker scored from close range to mark his third goal in three games and take an early 1-0 lead against Chicago. But at the end of a goal-heavy matchup, Lewandowski scored and assisted off the bench to help see the Fire to a 4-2 win. The Rapids ended the weekend in the final playoff position and have a tough final test against Dallas to hang on.

15. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 17

Cincinnati only forced one save out of Andre Blake, but with the help of Roman Celentano's six stops, they booked their playoff spot with a 1-0 win against the Union. Ayoub Jabbari came off the bench in the second half and registered the sole tally of the night, capitalizing on Blake's save (a low-struck ball from Evander) to score off the rebound.

16. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 16

The Dynamo could secure home advantage in the playoffs with a top-of-the-table finish, but are hanging on to fifth place ahead of the final day after losing 3-1 to Portland (their first loss in six). They have a decisive meeting with St. Louis on the final day, who are just ahead of them on goal difference but tied on points.

17. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 19

Sergi Roberto's first MLS goal was the icing on the cake of a 4-1 win against Austin that also featured Hirving Lozano's first goal back from injury and three assists from Marco Reus. Austin's not the toughest opponent in MLS this season, but the result matters as the Galaxy head into the final weekend still competing for a playoff spot.

18. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 20

The Crew may have lost the U.S. Open Cup final, but after beating D.C United 3-0, they're finishing the regular season on a five-game win streak. They confirmed their spot in the postseason and finished the weekend in one of the Eastern Conference's two wild card positions.

19. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 22

The Timbers secured a massive three points in a 3-1 win against the Dynamo highlighted by two assists and a goal from Vincent Janssen (nearly half his total goal contributions this year). With one game remaining, they're in a wild card spot and have one tentative hand on the playoffs.

20. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 23

In his first start since September, Joaquín Pereyra powered the Loons to three points with two goals against LAFC in a 3-1 win. They're still short of a final playoff spot (by two points) but following this result, they can still potentially break in with a win (and other results going in their favor), with San Jose waiting on the final day.

21. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 18

After falling behind 2-0 early to San Jose, Juan Manuel Sanabria's headed goal (his second of the year) in the 23rd minute provided life, but unfortunately nothing followed. They're currently outside the wild card spots ahead of a crucial final game against the Galaxy, but will also need some results to go their way.

22. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 12

RBNY had an early penalty stopped but came out with the upper hand against Nashville, taking a 2-0 lead in Tennessee that started with a beautiful link up between league wonderkids Adri Mehmeti and Julian Hall. But after two own goals and a stoppage-time winner from Nashville, the Red Bulls were eliminated from the playoffs in consecutive seasons for the first time ever.

23. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 21

After conceding a 91st-minute goal to last-placed Montréal, the Pigeons' playoff chances are officially over. A 1-1 draw isn't enough to launch them into the wild card position with one more game to go.

24. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 26

stories.headline: Kimi Antonelli is F1 champion. But why didn't he get his trophy in Mexico City?
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli is F1 world champion, but he won't get his trophy until December. Why does the sport still deny its champions their crowning moment?
stories.body:
There was one rather significant thing missing from Kimi Antonelli's world championship celebrations in Mexico City: the world championship trophy itself.

Despite becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history, the Italian will have to wait until Dec. 12 to get his hands on the prize he has spent his life chasing. That is because, unlike almost every other major sporting competition, F1 does not hand its championship trophy to the winner at the moment of victory. Instead, Antonelli will receive it while wearing a tuxedo, in a sterile hall, at the FIA's annual prize-giving gala dinner in Shanghai in December, six weeks after clinching the title.

It is one of F1's more peculiar traditions, denying the sport the sort of iconic sporting image synonymous with its biggest prizes. Think of the World Cup, the Super Bowl's Vince Lombardi Trophy or NHL's Stanley Cup, just to name three. The moment of triumph and the presentation of the trophy are inseparable. It doesn't have to be a conventional trophy, either. The Masters has turned the previous winner presenting the new winner a green blazer one of the most iconic images in all of sports.

F1's championship trophy, by contrast, seems almost an afterthought. Many fans would struggle to recognise it, which seems crazy for the series which is the pinnacle of motor racing.

It is a shame, too, because it is an impressive piece of silverware. Introduced in 1995, the trophy is made of sterling silver with gold detailing and features the signatures of Formula 1's world champions, stretching back to Giuseppe Farina in 1950.

So why wasn't it visible in Mexico City?

The answer lies in the divide between Formula 1 and its governing body, the FIA.

While F1, owned by Liberty Media, controls the commercial side of the championship, the FIA oversees its sporting and regulatory affairs. The world championship trophy falls under the FIA's jurisdiction -- Antonelli on Sunday officially became the FIA Formula 1 world champion - and its regulations stipulate that it must be presented at the governing body's annual gala.

Liberty Media has been keen to make more of the championship trophy. Sources have told ESPN discussions over a change this year did take place -- as they have for successive years now -- that the trophy be presented to Antonelli the moment he won it this year. However, as has also happened in previous seasons, it was agreed the FIA would stick with the convention of previous seasons and opt against doing anything radically different this time around.

- Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Verstappen wins Mexico City GP for Red Bull; Antonelli seals historic title

- Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

The FIA has long argued that presenting the trophy at its gala is important to the occasion's prestige. The event celebrates champions from across motorsport, including rallying, endurance racing and karting, with the presence of Formula 1's world champion regarded as an important attraction for the younger winners.

There is also a sporting justification, as race results can be challenged or altered after the chequered flag, potentially changing the outcome of a championship. The FIA prefers to wait until those matters are settled before handing over its biggest prize.

That argument has some merit, although less so when Antonelli has wrapped up the championship with four races still to run. It rather falls apart altogether when considering what happens at every grand prix as it is the exact opposite of the practice the FIA puts forward in that instance. Individual race trophies are handed out immediately after the finish, despite those results also being subject to protests, penalties and subsequent disqualifications. If a result changes, the trophies simply change hands.

Look no further than Sunday's race in Mexico City for an example. Antonelli was clutching his third-place Mexico City Grand Prix trophy in his hands at different points during his celebratory moments on the podium and the ceremony which followed. That despite the fact a post-race penalty or protest could have moved him down the order after the fact -- it wouldn't have stopped him being champion, but it would have meant he should not have been on the podium. And yet, he did not have the world championship trophy in his hand for that exact same reason.

There is little reason why the championship should be treated differently to an individual race, especially when the current practice stops the trophy becoming a prize that champions can share with fans in the celebratory moments.

It seems a missed opportunity for a sport which has spent the past decade transforming the way it presents itself to the world. F1 has embraced new audiences, new technology and new ways of celebrating its biggest moments, yet its most prestigious prize remains tied to an awards dinner.

Antonelli will undoubtedly enjoy getting his hands on the trophy in Shanghai. But the moment he became world champion, surrounded by his Mercedes team and thousands of celebrating fans in Mexico City, has already passed and it is a moment Formula 1 cannot recreate.

stories.headline: AFL 2027 fixture: Five must-watch games in the first month
stories.summary: The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month.
stories.body:
The 2027 AFL fixture has been released. So, to whet your appetite for the upcoming season, we've picked out the five must-watch games from the opening month of action.

Get the popcorn ready and get set to enjoy these absolute belters in the new year.

5. Port Adelaide vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 4, Adelaide Oval, Sunday, April 8, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Make no mistake, when Zak Butters returns to Adelaide Oval to face his old mob for the first time since departing, it's going to be incredibly spicy.

In a move that shocked absolutely nobody, Butters left Port Adelaide during the 2026 trade period, inking a long-term deal with the Western Bulldogs. It's a brutal blow for the Power, and his ex-teammates will be sure to give him a hard time when they share the field in Round 4. You just know it's going to be on for young and old!

The AFL also made the move to schedule this blockbuster game as the closer to next year's Gather Round. It means far more bodies will be in Adelaide that weekend and a greater number of eyeballs on the clash.

4. Hawthorn vs. Geelong - Round 2, MCG, Monday, March 29, 3:15pm (AEDT)
The traditional Easter Monday clash between the Hawks and Cats is always on our shortlist of early season must-watch games, and next year will be no exception.

Both of these clubs are in the premiership window. Both clubs have added high-profile players this offseason. Both clubs have fanbases that bring an electric energy to Easter Monday at the MCG.

This one is also set to be a fascinating coaching battle between Chris Scott and Sam Mitchell, two of the game's best tacticians, who will go head-to-head just as much as the players on the field.

3. Fremantle vs. Western Bulldogs - Round 1, Optus Stadium, Thursday, March 18, 8:10pm (AEDT)
This Round 1 game in the west is simply oozing with intrigue.

Of course, the question on everyone's mind is how the Dockers back up after having this year's premiership ripped away from them in harrowing circumstances. Does it galvanise the club? Will we see 'Wharfie Time'? Surely not!

For the Bulldogs, they landed the biggest fish of the off-season in superstar midfielder Zak Butters. This will be the first opportunity to watch him play in his new colours, lining up in the middle alongside skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards.

2. Brisbane vs. Collingwood - Round 2, Gabba, Thursday, March 25, 7:50pm (AEDT)
Reigning premier Brisbane will unfurl its latest flag in Round 2 when it hosts Collingwood in its first home game of the season, a clash that has blockbuster written all over it.

The Lions are looking to become just the second team ever to win four consecutive flags (joining, you guessed it, Collingwood from 1927 to 1930) but will be doing it without superstar midfielder Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow medallist departed for the Magpies this offseason, making this early season contest between the two clubs extra intriguing.

Plus, any opportunity to watch current Brownlow medallist Nick Daicos play footy is reason in itself to tune in!

1. Hawthorn vs. Brisbane - Round 1, MCG, Friday, March 19, 7:40pm (AEDT)
Thankfully we don't have to wait long for the Hawks and Lions -- quite possibly the competition's two best teams -- to square off in 2027. And if this game delivers even 70% of what these sides dished up in this year's epic preliminary final, then we're in for an absolute treat!

Many have labelled Brisbane's thrilling win over Hawthorn this past September as the greatest game of footy played this century. That in itself should be enough of a reason for their next clash to simply be must-watch.

There will be extra intrigue with both teams given this clash falls in Round 1. For the Lions, they will be looking to navigate life without both superstar midfielder Lachie Neale and master coach Chris Fagan, while the Hawks will be attempting to integrate recruits Zach Merrett and Ben King into their line-up.

stories.headline: Ponga back for NZ as Walsh wins Aussie fullback role
stories.summary: Australian coach Kevin Walters has shown his hand with a big fullback call as New Zealand superstar Kayln Ponga returns for the Rugby League World Cup semis.
stories.body:
Kayln Ponga and Reece Walsh are on track to resume their compelling rivalry after two huge coach calls ahead of the Rugby League World Cup semifinals.

Ponga has been named on New Zealand's extended bench for Saturday night's do-or-die showdown with Tonga in Newcastle, just 22 days after breaking his forearm in a dazzling fullback duel with Walsh in the tournament opener.

And Walsh on Tuesday retained the Australian No.1 jumper ahead of James Tedesco for the Kangaroos' semi-final against Samoa in Sydney on Sunday.

While young gun Keono Kini will again start as custodian at McDonald Jones Stadium, Ponga's inclusion is a firm indication the Newcastle Knights superstar will return for the final should the Kiwis make it.

Coach Stacey Jones also selected hooker Phoenix Crossland among the Kiwis' extended reserves as Australian Test coach Kevin Walters made the most significant move of his tenure by picking Walsh over Tedesco.

The selection dilemma has bubbled along through Australia's three group-stage wins.

Tedesco entered the World Cup in exceptional form after helping the Sydney Roosters to the NRL premiership, while Walsh had spent the last two months on the sidelines with an ankle injury.

But Walsh - the star of last year's Ashes series - has done enough to win the backing of former Broncos coach Walters for the business end of the tournament.

Walsh and Ponga were both electrifying in Australia's 24-22 win over New Zealand last month, before Walsh was man of the match with a hand in five tries in last Saturday's 66-6 rout of the Cook Islands.

In other key Australian selections, Bradman Best has made the left centre spot his own by seeing off the challenge of South Sydney talisman Latrell Mitchell.

Tedesco and Mitchell are both part of a six-man bench that includes Canberra's Ethan Strange and Cameron Murray for the likely Allianz Stadium sell-out.

Tom Dearden and Cameron Munster will line up together in the halves.

"Samoa were very impressive in a physical battle which had a lot of emotion last weekend against Tonga and we know we are in for a tough contest on Sunday night," Walters said.

"It's going to be a great occasion in front of a full house at Allianz Stadium, and we've got to meet the occasion with our best performance of the tournament."

Samoa have made just one enforced change with Ronald Volkman replacing Chanel Harris-Tavita (hamstring) at five-eighth.

In the other semi-final, Tonga are unchanged while Crossland remains an option to feature for the first time since his four-match suspension for his leg-breaking tackle on Nathan Cleary in the NRL preliminary final.

The Newcastle hooker was officially elevated to New Zealand's squad on Monday night after forward Jacob Laban was ruled out with injury.

Jones has named Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad on the wing as a result of Ronaldo Mulitalo's one-game ban for a shoulder charge against Fiji.
